title: Volume of Pyramids and Cones — Problems

problems.problem_text: Find the volume of a rectangular pyramid with base length 6 cm, width 5 cm, and height 9 cm.
Find the volume of a cone with radius 3 cm and height 7 cm (use pi = 22/7).
Find the volume of a square-based pyramid with base side 4 cm and height 6 cm.
problems.solution: Base area = 16 cm^2. V = (1/3) x 16 x 6 = 32 cm^3

problems.problem_text: Find the volume of a cone with diameter 10 cm and height 12 cm (use pi = 3.142).
A rectangular prism and a pyramid have the same base (8 cm by 5 cm) and same height (12 cm). How many times larger is the prism's volume?
A cone has volume 100 cm^3 and radius 5 cm. Find its height (use pi = 3.142).
A pyramid has a triangular base with base 6 cm and height 8 cm. The pyramid height is 10 cm. Find its volume.
An ice cream cone has radius 3 cm and height 15 cm. Find its volume (use pi = 3.142).
A square pyramid has volume 200 cm^3 and height 12 cm. Find the side length of its base.
A cone of radius 9 cm and height 18 cm is cut 6 cm from the top to form a frustum. The top cone (removed) has radius 3 cm and height 6 cm. Find the volume of the frustum (use pi = 3.142).
A cone has radius 4 cm and height 9 cm. If both radius and height are doubled, by what factor does the volume increase?
problems.solution: Original V = (1/3) pi x 16 x 9 = 48 pi. New: r=8, h=18. V = (1/3) pi x 64 x 18 = 384 pi. Ratio = 384/48 = 8

problems.problem_text: A rectangular pyramid has base 10 cm by 6 cm and volume 180 cm^3. Find its height.
problems.solution: Base area = 60 cm^2. V = (1/3) x 60 x h = 20h. 180 = 20h. h = 9 cm

problems.problem_text: A cone with radius 6 cm and a hemisphere of the same radius have equal volumes. Find the height of the cone (use pi = 3.142).
problems.solution: V_hemi = (2/3) pi r^3 = (2/3) pi x 216 = 144 pi. V_cone = (1/3) pi r^2 h = (1/3) pi x 36 x h = 12 pi h. 12 pi h = 144 pi. h = 12 cm

problems.problem_text: A frustum of a cone has top radius 2 cm, bottom radius 5 cm, and height 9 cm. Find its volume (use pi = 3.142).
problems.solution: Full cone: h = 9 x 5/(5-2) = 15 cm. V_full = (1/3) pi x 25 x 15 = 125 pi = 392.75. Small cone: V_small = (1/3) pi x 4 x 6 = 8 pi = 25.136. Frustum = 392.75 - 25.136 = 367.614. Wait let me recalculate properly with similar triangles. Full cone: bottom r=5, top r=2, frustum h=9. Using similar triangles: H_full/5 = (H_full-9)/2. 2H = 5H - 45, 3H = 45, H=15. Top cone height = 6. V_full = (1/3) pi x 25 x 15 = 125 pi = 392.75. V_top = (1/3) pi x 4 x 6 = 8 pi = 25.136. Frustum = 392.75 - 25.136 = 367.614 cm^3

problems.problem_text: Pyramid A has base 6 cm by 6 cm and height 10 cm. Pyramid B has base 12 cm by 12 cm and height 20 cm. What is the ratio of their volumes?
A cone of radius 5 cm and height 15 cm is full of water. Water is poured out until the depth is 10 cm. What fraction of the water remains?
problems.solution: Full cone: r=5, h=15. When depth=10, the remaining water forms a smaller cone similar to the original. Height ratio = 10/15 = 2/3. Radius ratio = 2/3. Volume ratio = (2/3)^3 = 8/27.
